lessons.title: The Rich Don't Work for Money
lessons.key_idea: Through young Robert's low-paid job at rich dad's store, the book shows how fear and desire keep people chasing paychecks, and why learning to make money work for you is the way out of the rat race.

lessons.title: Buy Assets, Not Liabilities
lessons.key_idea: Wealth comes from building a column of assets that put money in your pocket, like businesses and rental property, rather than buying liabilities, including a home you live in, which take money out.

plan.title: Rich Dad Poor Dad: What the Rich Teach Their Kids About Money That the Poor and Middle Class Do Not!
plan.author: Robert T. Kiyosaki (with Sharon Lechter)
plan.confidence_note: I know this book's core lessons, framing and main stories in detail, though I avoid fine specifics I can't verify.
plan.one_liner: Two fathers, two money mindsets, and why working harder alone rarely makes anyone rich.
plan.summary: Robert Kiyosaki tells the story of growing up in Hawaii with two father figures. His own father was highly educated and held a respected government job, yet he struggled with money all his life. His best friend's father left school early but built real wealth through businesses and property. Through the lessons of this rich dad, Kiyosaki argues that schools teach people to work for money but rarely teach how money actually works. He urges readers to learn the difference between assets, which put money in your pocket, and liabilities, which take money out. He warns that fear and desire keep people trapped in a cycle of earning and spending that he calls the rat race. His answer is financial literacy, steadily building assets, and choosing work for what it teaches rather than just the paycheck.
